$note: Measured scale baseline for the components PERF-002 names, plus DiffViewer. Written by src/__tests__/performance/scale.test.tsx, which asserts every budget below; validated by scripts/check/performance.mjs, which refuses a raised one.
environment: vitest 4 + jsdom, Node 20+. jsdom does no layout and no paint: getBoundingClientRect is all zeros and ResizeObserver never fires. Every number here is JavaScript work and DOM construction, NOT browser rendering performance. A component that is cheap here can still be slow to paint.

metrics.elements: DOM elements the mounted component built, container included (container.querySelectorAll('*').length).
metrics.dataReads: Reads of the component's input: index reads on the array prop, or field reads on its items where the component copies the array first. Counted through a Proxy, so it is exact and machine-independent — which makes the growth between two fixture sizes a complexity assertion rather than a timing guess. Omitted where the input is not an array.
metrics.listeners: addEventListener calls during mount, beyond the ~140 React 19 delegates to every container. 0 means the component adds no native listeners of its own.

policy: A ratchet, not a target. Each budget is the value measured on the date below plus headroom: 10% rounded up for counts of 20 or more, exact below that (where 10% is noise). Budgets may only shrink. scripts/check/performance.mjs fails a commit that raises one, drops a case, or parks a budget more than 25% above its measurement — a budget nobody has to meet is not a budget.
recording: Run `bunx vitest run src/__tests__/performance/scale.test.tsx`; the failure message carries the measured value. Update `measured` and `budget` together, and say why in the changeset.

tree-view/roots-20-children-5-collapsed.$dataReads: Re-recorded 2026-08-22: was {'measured': 22, 'budget': 25}. TreeView now resolves reading direction, and when no DirectionProvider is present that resolution reads the DOM in a layout effect, so the subtree renders once more before paint and every node's data is read twice. The extra pass is the documented cost of keeping the first render identical on server and client (see useResolvedDirection); wrapping the tree in a DirectionProvider removes it entirely, because steps 1 and 2 of resolution are available during render. The DOM-count invariant this case exists for -- collapsed subtrees are not rendered -- is unchanged.
